dtc_hex_74_10_4.name: dtc_hex_74_10_4
dtc_hex_74_10_4.d_method: method not stated for this table; the paper's only statement on distance computation (App. B, Table III caption) is integer programming, which terminated for distances <= 20, and QDistRnd upper bounds above 20; all values here are <= 15, so presumably exact IP values
dtc_hex_74_10_4.notes: (M,N) = (4,2), word ENES2WS2ENE. square-lattice tile code of ENES2WS2ENE; the hexagonal grid enters only through the hardware embedding (Fig. 3, degree-3 brick-wall graph, drawn rotated by 90 degrees). The paper gives no M, N for hexagonal codes. MISMATCH: n = 74 is not reachable: for this word n = ((2x+3)(2y+7) - 1)/2 with x = N+1 columns and y = M+1 rows, and 2*74+1 = 149 is prime; no rotation or reflection of the word helps either. Built at (M,N) = (4,2), n = 76, the step between [[52,10,3]] at (3,1) and [[104,10,5]] at (5,3); the other near sizes are n = 73 at (6,1) and n = 77 at (11,0). The paper's 74 may be a typo for 76: the square w = 9 family obeys the same n formula with M and N exchanged and has [[76,10,4]] at the mirrored size (2,4). Whether this matrix has d = 4 is not established.
